title: Rice, white, with gravy, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Rice, white, with gravy, no added fat is boiled white rice served with a light sauce prepared without oil or butter. The dish is often used in diet plans because it provides minimal fat while delivering a quick source of energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: White rice is one of the most widely consumed grains worldwide.
When cooked properly, rice retains most of its carbohydrates but virtually no fat.
Fat‑free gravy is usually made from broth, tomatoes, or aromatic spices.
Rice appears in traditional dishes across Asia, Europe, and the Americas, adapted for low‑fat diets.
Compared with whole‑grain rice, white rice has a softer texture and cooks faster.

items.title: Fast energy source
items.content: White rice is rich in carbohydrates that quickly convert to glucose, providing immediate energy.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: A fat‑free preparation makes the dish suitable for low‑fat dietary regimens and helps control calorie intake.

items.title: Easy to digest
items.content: Boiled rice is gentle on the stomach, making it appropriate for people with sensitive digestion.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Rice provides thiamine (B1), niacin (B3) and folate, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports hydration
items.content: Cooked in water, rice retains moisture that contributes to overall fluid balance.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: White rice can raise blood sugar quickly, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Low fiber content
items.content: Unlike whole‑grain rice, white rice provides little dietary fiber, which may affect digestive health.

items.title: Possible arsenic content
items.content: In some regions rice can accumulate arsenic; choose reputable sources to minimize exposure.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the rice as a side dish with vegetables, lean fish, or poultry. Add the fat‑free gravy just before serving to preserve flavor. Fresh herbs, lemon juice, or spices can be added for extra taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store dry rice in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. Cooked rice should be cooled quickly and kept in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.
